subject: Pilot packaging and tier swap — bundling options for CrowdWell
messages:
From: Maya Jennings <maya.j@crowdwell.com>

Cc: legal@crowdwell.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging options for pilot + potential tier swap

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. Our product team liked the latency profile and the prefix caching example. Before we move forward with a pilot, we need clarity on packaging. A few specific asks:

- We want to run a 3-month pilot with 50k generation tokens/day and embeddings for search vectors (~1M embeddings/month). Which plan best maps to that usage?
- Is there a recommended approach for a temporary tier upgrade (2 months) and then automatic step-down to a lower tier? Will we be prorated or keep credits?
- Can certain add-on features (KV-cache persist, higher retention in logs) be purchased a la carte for the pilot?

Also, our legal team will likely ask for an SOW and a clear cost table we can attach to the purchase order. Can you send a short options matrix (price + outcome) and call out any minimum commitment?

Appreciate it — can we aim to finalize the pilot packaging this week?

Best,
Maya Jennings
Head of Product
CrowdWell

Attachments: sample-traffic.csv (referenced)
From: ethan_park@redwood.ai
To: Maya Jennings <maya.j@crowdwell.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 12:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging options for pilot + potential tier swap

Hi Maya —

Thanks — really glad the team liked the demo. I sketched 3 feasible pilot configurations (attached pricing_grid_CW_v2.xlsx) — quick summary below so you can share with legal/product: 

Option A — Elastic Pilot (no commit)- Short description: usage-metered, best if traffic uncertain.- Cost: per-token and per-embedding unit; forecasted ~ $X/day for 50k tokens + embedding unit tiers.- Pros: no commitment, immediate start.- Cons: higher unit cost, no dedicated burst.

Option B — Reserved Pilot (3-month commit, step-down friendly)- Short description: 3-month reserved capacity with an explicit 2-month temporary "upgrade window".- Cost: lower per-token equivalent; includes a one-time pilot discount (10% off list) tied to the reserved amount.- Step-down behavior: we support an automatic tier step-down at the end of month 2; unused reserved tokens are credited toward subsequent months within the pilot window (proration applies per SOW).

Option C — Dedicated Mini-Pool (for stability)- Short description: Dedicated GPU pool for the pilot; recommended only if you need strict latency/throughput SLOs.- Cost: fixed monthly commitment, includes priority routing and KV-cache persistence add-on.

Add-ons
- KV-cache persistence (30-day): available a la carte.
- Extended log retention (90-day): available as an add-on; pricing shown in the sheet.

Next steps I recommend:
1) If you want an easy start, pick Option B (Reserved Pilot) — it balances cost and guarantees.
2) We can include a clause in the SOW that allows a one-time temporary upgrade window (2 months) with automatic step-down and clear proration.
3) I'll loop in Lauren for approval on the pilot discount and Ben for implementation notes.

I attached a draft SOW and the pricing grid. Let me know 2 preferred start dates and whether CrowdWell requires vendor legal redlines before we ship the SOW.

Thanks,
Ethan Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_grid_CW_v2.xlsx, SOW_CrowdWell_v1.pdf

Looping in pricing — I reviewed Ethan's sheet. We can approve a 10% pilot discount on Option B for CrowdWell. A few guardrails:

- Discount max applies to the committed reserved tokens only (not metered overages).
- The temporary upgrade window should have a clear upper bound (we recommend setting an explicit token cap during the 2-month upgrade to avoid runaway spend).
- Proration logic: unused reserved tokens during month 1 can be carried to month 2 of the pilot; any unused after month 3 are forfeited unless CrowdWell converts to a committed annual contract.

Ethan — I'll sign off on the SOW once you include the upgrade cap and the carry-forward proration language. Ben, please add a short bullet about how we instrument the KV-cache persistence as an add-on (what toggles, expected costs).

Thanks,
